Get ready to “feel it all over.”

This week, Stevie Wonder kicks off the North American leg of his highly anticipated Songs In The Key of Life 50th Anniversary Tour.

The 25-time Grammy winner has just four U.S. concerts celebrating his seminal 1976 record. They’re scheduled to take place at:

Madison Square GardenNew York, NYThursday, Nov. 19United CenterChicago, ILSaturday, Nov. 21Capital One ArenaWashington, D.C.Monday, Nov. 23Intuit DomeInglewood, CASaturday, Dec. 19

If you’d like to see the timeless hitmaker deliver the songs you know and love live, last-minute tickets are still available.

At the time of publication, the lowest price we could find on seats for any one show was $344 including fees on Vivid Seats.

Tickets start at $987 including fees for the MSG gig.

According to Set List FM, the 76-year-old crooner played 24 songs per show, at his recent European concerts.

That included both sides of “Songs In The Key of Life,” which features classic tracks “Isn’t She Lovely,” “I Wish,” “As,” “Pastime Paradise” and, of course, “Sir Duke.”

Records indicate he also busted out his fan favorite smashes “Superstition” and “I Was Made To Love Her” as well as covers of John Lennon’s “Imagine” and Michael Jackson’s “Billie Jean.”

“You spend a lot of the show with your jaw on the floor,” The Guardian wrote in a five-star review of a recent show at Great Britain’s Utilita Arena.

“Even given its reputation, Songs in the Key of Life still has the ability to knock you sideways with the astonishing level of quality it maintains throughout: it’s an album on which the deep cuts would be anyone else’s showstoppers.”

Don’t miss out. This show sounds special.

For more information, our team has everything you need to know and more about Stevie Wonder’s 2026 Songs In The Key of Life 50th Anniversary Tour below.

A complete calendar including all North American tour dates, venues and links to the cheapest tickets available can be found here:

Set List FM reports these are the 24 tracks that Wonder took to the stage at a recent gig in Glasgow, Scotland.

01.) “Love’s in Need of Love Today”

02.) “Have a Talk With God” (With Mandla Morris)

03.) “Village Ghetto Land”

07.) “Knocks Me Off My Feet”

08.) “It’s Easier / I Was Made to Love Her / Jam / Billie Jean” (Live debut of It’s Easier, first time I Was Made to Love Her was played since 2024)

15.) “Joy Inside My Tears”

18.) “Easy Goin’ Evening (My Mama’s Call)”

19.) “Ngiculela – Es Una Historia – I Am Singing”

20.) “If It’s Magic” (With Brandee Younger on harp)

22.) “Imagine” (John Lennon cover) (with Zaiah Morris) (Sung by Zaiah Morris)

According to the Instagram account @StevieWonderLegacy (which is not Wonder’s official profile), he does. They wrote:

More than two decades after “A Time to Love,” Stevie Wonder says a new album is coming in 2027. The title has been circulating for years. “Through the Eyes of Wonder” has surfaced, disappeared, been reshaped, then mentioned again. At some point it stopped feeling like a record and started to feel like a rumor. Now it finally has a horizon.Part of the pull comes from what might be inside. Early reports suggest unreleased material from the Songs in the Key of Life period, which complicates the idea of a “new” Stevie Wonder album. This isn’t just a late-career statement. It’s potentially a splice between eras, between a creative peak that still defines the genre and a present that has mostly unfolded off record.After Characters (1987), the releases thinned out. Not a collapse, more a withdrawal. Fewer albums, longer gaps, a shift away from the studio as the primary space of expression. The catalog froze in time while the reputation kept expanding. That’s what makes this different. Not the possibility of another hit, not even the idea of a comeback. Just the fact that he’s choosing to add something new to a body of work that has, for a long time, felt complete.

Many iconic artists that defined the Motown, soul, funk and R&B sounds of the late 20th century are still going strong.

Here are just five of our favorites playing live these next few months that you won’t want to miss.

• The Temptations and The Four Tops

Who else is out and about? Take a look at this list of all of the biggest R&B icons on tour in 2026 to find the show for you.

This article was written by Matt Levy, New York Post live events reporter. Levy stays up-to-date on all the latest tour announcements from your favorite musical artists and comedians, as well as Broadway openings, sporting events and more live shows – and finds great ticket prices online. Since he started his tenure at the Post in 2022, Levy has reviewed a Bruce Springsteen concert and interviewed Melissa Villaseñor of SNL fame, to name a few. Please note that deals can expire, and all prices are subject to change.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

For us guys, losing testosterone is a lot like losing our hair. By the time we really notice it, a lot more is gone than we realize.

I’m in my 40s, which is right about when the math starts to catch up. Men’s testosterone levels slide roughly 1% a year starting somewhere between 30 and 40, according to Cleveland Clinic and Mayo Clinic.

There’s no cliff and no “male menopause” moment. It’s a slow leak, and Mayo says most older men stay in the normal range anyway.

I rank as one of the normal ones. My first blood test in March came back at 430, the lower end of normal, against a lab range of 249 to 836 ng/dL. Low, but fine.

It isn’t. There’s no testosterone in the bottle. But I think that’s a good thing.

Hims Testosterone Rx is a prescription tablet of enclomiphene, a drug that nudges your brain into telling your body to make more of its own.

“Enclomiphene works by encouraging the pituitary, which is the part of the brain that controls testicular function, to send stronger hormonal signals through the bloodstream to the testicles,” Dr. Peter Stahl, senior vice president of sexual health at Hims, told The Post. “These stronger signals boost testicular production of testosterone.”

Traditional TRT, the shots and gels, adds testosterone from the outside. Your body can notice and slow its own production, and sperm count can go along with it.

“The brain senses sufficient testosterone onboard and reacts by turning off the signaling that drives testicular function,” Stahl said. “That shuts down the two things that the testicles do: making testosterone and producing sperm.”

In two Phase 3 trials, men on enclomiphene kept their sperm counts while men on testosterone gel saw theirs fall, researchers reported in BJU International. Stahl, who also treats male infertility, said enclomiphene and its parent drug, clomiphene, “are sometimes prescribed by male infertility experts like me as off-label treatment for male infertility.”

That, and no needles, makes this an easy add to a daily routine.

Two things to know before you get excited. The pill is compounded, which means it is not FDA-approved, and Hims makes that clear right in the app. After the influx of GLP-1 and injectable peptides, compounded medications are becoming less and less rare and more understood. It also isn’t sold in all 50 states.

Stahl’s advice for anyone uneasy about that: “What matters is who is prescribing, what testing came first, and whether there’s follow-up.” He added that “the evidence base is smaller than for TRT, and a good clinician will say so.”

However, since I started this medication, Hims has started to offer real TRT:

I’m not squeamish about blood, which wouldn’t really matter with the low level I was working with here. The kit that shows up is a little red-button gadget you stick on your upper arm. Press it, hear (and feel) the click, wait a few minutes while the tube fills, peel it off. Do it again on the other arm.

It didn’t hurt. It barely bled. If you’ve ever done a finger-prick test and winced every time you typed for the next couple days, this is different. The directions were clear and I never messed up a sample.

I mailed my first kit back and had results in the app a couple days later. A provider signed off, the prescription was ordered March 11, and the bottle hit my mailbox March 16.

Every bit of care communication happens via the app’s messaging platform. No video or no phone. None that I have been offered anyway. I heard from a different nurse practitioner or doctor almost every time, and replies were quick. When I needed my address changed, it took a couple of hours.

Three months of one pill a day and I was at 1,273. That’s well past the top of the lab’s range. By September it was over 1,500, the point where the lab stops counting.

According to Stahl, that kind of jump happens.

“When the brain’s signal is switched back on, some men respond strongly in the first few weeks, and levels can sometimes peak early at a higher level than where they ultimately settle,” he said. “That’s not the most common pattern, but it definitely occurs in some patients.”

This is where Hims earned some respect. That September result posted at lunchtime. By 7 p.m., a nurse practitioner was asking how often I was taking it. By 9:18 p.m., a second NP and a doctor had weighed in, told me to stop the pills and ordered an immediate retest.

The October retest came in at 694. Dead center of healthy. I’m back on every other day.

That last panel also showed my hematocrit at 37.9%, under the lab’s floor of 40.1%. A Hims doctor flagged it as possible anemia and told me to take it to my primary care doctor. Since my doctor of 20 years just retired this fall, I am on the hunt for a new one.

It’s one of the numbers Hims watches on purpose. “Hematocrit and PSA (for older men) are essential for safety and need to be regularly monitored,” Stahl said.

This is not a pop-it-and-forget-it pill. The blood tests are crucial. Mine came every three or so months, and Stahl said the standard schedule is “at baseline, again within the first couple of months, then at least annually.”

I’m still tired all the time. I have sleep issues, which is a separate problem that no little pill was going to fix. I do the elliptical and lift, and the lifting feels a bit better; recovery too. Not enough that I’d make it the focus of my review.

I notice I am far less sore if I take time off from lifting or if I up my weight that day.

Turns out a big number and a small payoff is a known thing. Stahl said TRT can be “the better choice for patients who have tried enclomiphene but didn’t feel better on it, even if their testosterone level on their blood work improved a lot.”

“This can happen in some cases because some men respond unpredictably to the anti-estrogen effect of enclomiphene, which is not an issue with TRT,” he said.

I also had zero side effects. None, even when I was living my best life above 1,500. Hims lists headaches, nausea, hot flashes, mood changes and, rarely, vision changes as possibilities.

As for how much is known about taking it for years, Stahl didn’t sugarcoat it. “Not as much as we’d like,” he said. “The largest controlled enclomiphene trials lasted 16 weeks.”

“I’d rather say that plainly than overstate what we know, and it’s why ongoing monitoring isn’t optional,” he added.

So pop these pills at your own risk I suppose.

After 8 months and four blood tests, the pill did exactly what it promised on paper but less in real life. Here’s what worked for me and what didn’t:

It cost me $990, paid upfront, for 10 months. That’s a lot of money to say I feel a little better at the gym.

The app doesn’t help its own case. It works, but it’s not built for jumping around. Everything is in there. You just have to go hunting. One thing about the app that really sticks in my craw is that I cannot remove past medications I have used that I discontinued, and it definitely wants me to explore all the other healthy life and longevity add-ons it offers.

If you want to feel 25 again before the weekend, maybe not. However, I went in without that as my plan.

If you’re a guy around my age whose numbers are drifting and you’d rather deal with it before it’s really a problem, I think it is.

It isn’t for everybody. Stahl said the ideal candidate is “a man with symptoms and confirmed low testosterone” whose body can still make its own, especially one who wants to protect his fertility. Men at higher risk for blood clots, with significant liver disease or with a history of prostate or male breast cancer should skip it, he said.

I look at this less like a treatment and more like prevention. I’m losing about 1% a year whether I pay attention or not, and I’d rather be at 694 than wherever I was headed.

Stahl would back me up there. The biggest myth about low T, he said, is “that it’s just a normal part of getting older and that men have to live with it.”

I wish I’d started sooner. My plan renews Dec. 26 and I fully intend on sticking with it. I’ll call it my little Christmas gift to myself.

Hims Testosterone Rx is a prescription treatment designed to address low testosterone levels. Delivered in a convenient oral pill format, this medication helps restore natural energy, increase muscle mass, and improve overall male vitality.

The pill works on paper, almost too well. My testosterone went from 430 ng/dL to over 1,500 ng/dL, got shut off for a few weeks and came back down to 694. I felt a little better in the gym but not like I turned all superhero overnight. I’m renewing anyway.

Hims Erectile Dysfunction treatments offer fast-acting, FDA-approved medications like sildenafil and tadalafil in chewable mints to improve blood flow for stronger, longer-lasting erections.

Hims Hair Loss treatments feature clinically proven ingredients like minoxidil to reactivate hair follicles and stimulate regrowth in 3 to 6 months.

Hims Weight Loss provides access to effective GLP-1 medications like weekly semaglutide injections. These treatments curb cravings and suppress appetite to promote long-term weight management.

No, and neither is enclomiphene anywhere else. A drugmaker called Repros Therapeutics tried to get it approved for low testosterone under the name Androxal. The FDA turned it down in December 2015, saying the trials weren’t built to prove a real clinical benefit, and it still isn’t approved today. What Hims ships is a compounded version, made by a pharmacy and legal with a prescription, but never reviewed by the FDA for safety or effectiveness. Hims says so in its own app, and it’s printed on my bottle. If the FDA stamp matters to you, Hims also sells Kyzatrex, an oral testosterone approved in July 2022, and generic testosterone cypionate injections. Both are actual testosterone, with everything that comes with it.

Think of it as Rogaine for your balls. Stop taking it, and lose everything it provided. So, if you want that higher number, yes. The pill doesn’t fix anything for good. It turns the signal up while you’re taking it. In one small 2013 study of 12 men, testosterone was back to where it started a month after they stopped. A Hims doctor paused my pills in September and I went from over 1,500 to 694 in 18 days. Plan on blood tests for as long as you’re on it, too. I did 4 in eight months.

No, but testosterone is. Congress put anabolic steroids, testosterone included, on Schedule III in 1990, the same tier as ketamine, which is why TRT comes with tighter prescribing rules. Enclomiphene isn’t a steroid and isn’t testosterone. You still need a prescription, and in my case, Hims didn’t write one until it had my bloodwork.

I’m still tired all the time. I have sleep issues, which is a separate problem that no little pill was going to fix. I do the elliptical and lift, and the lifting feels a bit better; recovery too. Not enough that I’d make it the focus of my review.

I notice I am far less sore if I take time off from lifting or if I up my weight that day.

Turns out a big number and a small payoff is a known thing. Stahl said TRT can be “the better choice for patients who have tried enclomiphene but didn’t feel better on it, even if their testosterone level on their blood work improved a lot.”

“This can happen in some cases because some men respond unpredictably to the anti-estrogen effect of enclomiphene, which is not an issue with TRT,” he said.

I also had zero side effects. None, even when I was living my best life above 1,500. Hims lists headaches, nausea, hot flashes, mood changes and, rarely, vision changes as possibilities.

As for how much is known about taking it for years, Stahl didn’t sugarcoat it. “Not as much as we’d like,” he said. “The largest controlled enclomiphene trials lasted 16 weeks.”

“I’d rather say that plainly than overstate what we know, and it’s why ongoing monitoring isn’t optional,” he added.

So pop these pills at your own risk I suppose.

After 8 months and four blood tests, the pill did exactly what it promised on paper but less in real life. Here’s what worked for me and what didn’t:

It cost me $990, paid upfront, for 10 months. That’s a lot of money to say I feel a little better at the gym.

The app doesn’t help its own case. It works, but it’s not built for jumping around. Everything is in there. You just have to go hunting. One thing about the app that really sticks in my craw is that I cannot remove past medications I have used that I discontinued, and it definitely wants me to explore all the other healthy life and longevity add-ons it offers.

If you want to feel 25 again before the weekend, maybe not. However, I went in without that as my plan.

If you’re a guy around my age whose numbers are drifting and you’d rather deal with it before it’s really a problem, I think it is.

It isn’t for everybody. Stahl said the ideal candidate is “a man with symptoms and confirmed low testosterone” whose body can still make its own, especially one who wants to protect his fertility. Men at higher risk for blood clots, with significant liver disease or with a history of prostate or male breast cancer should skip it, he said.

I look at this less like a treatment and more like prevention. I’m losing about 1% a year whether I pay attention or not, and I’d rather be at 694 than wherever I was headed.

Stahl would back me up there. The biggest myth about low T, he said, is “that it’s just a normal part of getting older and that men have to live with it.”

I wish I’d started sooner. My plan renews Dec. 26 and I fully intend on sticking with it. I’ll call it my little Christmas gift to myself.

Hims Testosterone Rx is a prescription treatment designed to address low testosterone levels. Delivered in a convenient oral pill format, this medication helps restore natural energy, increase muscle mass, and improve overall male vitality.

The pill works on paper, almost too well. My testosterone went from 430 ng/dL to over 1,500 ng/dL, got shut off for a few weeks and came back down to 694. I felt a little better in the gym but not like I turned all superhero overnight. I’m renewing anyway.

Hims Erectile Dysfunction treatments offer fast-acting, FDA-approved medications like sildenafil and tadalafil in chewable mints to improve blood flow for stronger, longer-lasting erections.

Hims Hair Loss treatments feature clinically proven ingredients like minoxidil to reactivate hair follicles and stimulate regrowth in 3 to 6 months.

Hims Weight Loss provides access to effective GLP-1 medications like weekly semaglutide injections. These treatments curb cravings and suppress appetite to promote long-term weight management.

No, and neither is enclomiphene anywhere else. A drugmaker called Repros Therapeutics tried to get it approved for low testosterone under the name Androxal. The FDA turned it down in December 2015, saying the trials weren’t built to prove a real clinical benefit, and it still isn’t approved today. What Hims ships is a compounded version, made by a pharmacy and legal with a prescription, but never reviewed by the FDA for safety or effectiveness. Hims says so in its own app, and it’s printed on my bottle. If the FDA stamp matters to you, Hims also sells Kyzatrex, an oral testosterone approved in July 2022, and generic testosterone cypionate injections. Both are actual testosterone, with everything that comes with it.

Think of it as Rogaine for your balls. Stop taking it, and lose everything it provided. So, if you want that higher number, yes. The pill doesn’t fix anything for good. It turns the signal up while you’re taking it. In one small 2013 study of 12 men, testosterone was back to where it started a month after they stopped. A Hims doctor paused my pills in September and I went from over 1,500 to 694 in 18 days. Plan on blood tests for as long as you’re on it, too. I did 4 in eight months.

No, but testosterone is. Congress put anabolic steroids, testosterone included, on Schedule III in 1990, the same tier as ketamine, which is why TRT comes with tighter prescribing rules. Enclomiphene isn’t a steroid and isn’t testosterone. You still need a prescription, and in my case, Hims didn’t write one until it had my bloodwork.

NEW ORLEANS — Yaxel Lendeborg, the typically talkative Warriors rookie, was given the night off Monday from his usual postgame media obligations.

He didn’t need to say a word to convey his feelings in Golden State’s 115-94 loss to the Pelicans. His body language came with as much candor as anything to escape his mouth.

Lendeborg poured in a team-high 28 points, but almost all of them came after the Warriors had dug themselves into a 31-point hole to a team that had lost its previous six games.

He spent the final minutes of the loss sitting on the bench, head hanging, with a towel covering his newly buzzed head of hair. Draymond Green picked up the slack with reporters after the game, and said that’s exactly what the Warriors need to do to help the rookie on the court.

“[We need to] depend on him, but lower the expectations,” Green said.

Fourteen games into his NBA career, the 24-year-old Michigan product is being asked to be the primary scorer in an offense with precious few options without Stephen Curry.

Green sees it taking a toll.

“It’s unfair to him to try to make him step into Steph’s role 13 games into his career. So depend on him like we need to, but lower what we expect of him to allow things to just flow into him.

“I think, right now, we’re putting too much pressure on him.”

All eyes were already on Lendeborg as soon as he stepped into Smoothie King Center. Taking the court for warm-ups, he unraveled a durag on his head and revealed his brand-new, chopped-off hair.

Lendeborg’s decision to lop off his lengthy locks came in response to an even more frustrating loss two nights earlier to the Spurs. He said afterward that the 48-point rout left him “f—ked up mentally.” Kerr emphasized the importance of quickly moving on to the next one of 82.

After a 1-of-13 shooting performance Saturday night, Lendeborg came out tepid, passive and generally a mess on both sides of the ball. He turned the ball over as many times as he shot it in the first quarter and racked up a minus-25 differential by halftime in a 61-36 game.

He was visibly frustrated at times, just like two nights earlier, but coach Steve Kerr didn’t think it was a product of Lendeborg’s emotions bleeding over from the San Antonio loss.

“I thought he was frustrated because we were getting killed again,” Kerr said. “He came over at one point and talked to me about some strategic stuff and made some really good adjustments at halftime and found his angles to attack.”

Lendeborg scored 20 on 7-of-14 shooting after halftime, but that was too little, too late.

He knew it. And so did the world. Because he showed as much.

“It’s his first year, and we’re putting an enormous responsibility on his shoulders,” coach Steve Kerr said. “He has to go through this. There’s no way around it. You can’t cheat your way through that. You have to feel the highs and the lows. You heard his comments the other night. He cares about all this stuff, which is a great sign. But you have to learn how to manage that.”

Green, who also doesn’t often lack for words, kept it concise when asked about Lendeborg’s night. Multiple times, he went up to the rookie with apparent words of advice.

“Just gotta play,” Green said.

“Just about how he’s got to play with Steph not out there,” he said.

It seemed to be a concerted effort on Green’s part to tamp down the attention on Lendeborg, which he has rightfully earned with his Rookie-of-the-Year worthy play but also comes with certain expectations. The pressure only rises without Curry, his 30 points per game and gravity.

The spotlight is going to continue to follow him.

Internally, at least, the Warriors are in control of the dimmer switch.

“We can control what we can control,” Green said. “We can’t control the [outside] world.”

Tulsa King is all about family, so it makes sense that the series star/EP Sylvester Stallone would want his real-life daughter, Scarlet Stallone, close by. After starring on the show for 4 seasons, the now 24-year-old has evolved on-screen right alongside her character, Spencer.

When we first met Spencer back in Season 1, she was a barista who endeared herself to Dwight Manfredi (Stallone) so much that, through Season 2, she worked as a horse caretaker at Manfredi’s Fennario Ranch. In Season 3, Spencer teamed up with Tyson (Jay Will) and Goodie (Chris Caldovino) to sell ecstasy.

“I would say I’m a very Season 3 girl at heart,” said Scarlet when she visited the Decider studio alongside Tulsa King co-star Garrett Hedlund earlier this month. “I’m a crazy wild child who takes risks here and there.”

In Season 4, after Dwight’s girlfriend/ranch co-owner Margaret Devereaux (Dana Delany) dies in a plane crash, Spencer is given the opportunity by Dwight to run Fennario Ranch. Much to her own surprise, Spencer thrives as the boss, especially with the support she receives from Mitch Keller (Hedlund) and the rest of the Manfredi crew.

Off-screen, Scarlet is supported by her proud father and vice versa. “I’ve been looking up to him my whole life,” said Scarlet. “We both know getting to work together on this show is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity that we’re never gonna have again.”

“We don’t have a lot of scenes together,” continued Scarlet, noting that both she and her father do their best to “take in those moments” together. Scarlet also noted that her dad freely “gives [her] advice” on set. “I don’t give him advice because he definitely knows what he’s doing,” said Scarlet with a laugh. “It doesn’t feel like work with him.”

And their father-daughter bond is apparent during filming, according to Hedlund. “Seeing how Sly is with her is beautiful,” said Hedlund, describing him as “protective,” “tender,” and “generous.” With Season 5 currently filming in NYC, the Stallones will have many special moments, both on and off set, to come.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The couple who Rex Ryan allegedly ran over earlier this month was livid with the former NFL head coach in the immediate aftermath of the incident, new police audio obtained by the California Post reveals.

Michael Holland, an attorney, and his wife dialed 911 just before midnight on Nov. 5 and told dispatch Ryan plowed into them while they were crossing Nashville’s famed Broadway street.

“I just got, literally, my wife and I both got ran over by some a—hole on f—king Broadway and I want to turn him in,” Holland said, according to the audio.

Holland answered multiple questions about the incident, and made it clear in each one of his responses that he was furious with Ryan over the matter.

“He f—king needs to be arrested,” Holland said, before he added that Ryan “was just a d—khead” who “needs to not be driving.”

When asked what kind of vehicle Ryan was in, Holland took another shot at the ex-Jets head coach.

“A big red pickup truck with oversized wheels that said small penis,” he said.

Holland then explained that the license plate was a New York one that read, “HIT QBS.”

Holland told dispatch he did not need an ambulance, though he did say it “f—king hurt.”

“My toes are going to be a mess tomorrow,” he added.

Police ultimately arrived on the scene, and following an investigation into Holland’s claims, six misdemeanor warrants charging Ryan with counts of leaving the scene of an accident, failure to give information/render aid, and failure to obey a traffic control signal were filed.

Ryan surrendered to authorities on Nov. 11 and was eventually released on $6,000 bond.

Court records show he’s due for a hearing in the case on Dec. 18.

Despite the arrest, Ryan appeared in his regular role as an analyst for ESPN on Sunday and Monday, but he did not address the incident while on the network’s airwaves.

TMZ was first to publish the 911 audio.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

San Francisco’s housing market is on fire — and wealthy buyers are leading the charge.

The city saw a record-breaking surge in luxury home sales in October, with nine single-family properties selling for more than $10 million and 40 fetching upward of $5 million, according to a new report from Compass.

Both figures marked the highest monthly totals since Multiple Listing Service records began in 1993, as deep-pocketed buyers snapped up high-end properties amid a dwindling supply of homes.

The $5 million-plus deals accounted for nearly 16% of the city’s 253 single-family sales in October.

The frenzy comes as San Francisco’s booming artificial intelligence industry fuels a mansion shortage, with newly wealthy tech executives and investors competing for a limited supply of luxury properties.

And the buying spree is pushing prices higher across the board.

San Francisco’s median single-family sale price jumped 29% year-over-year to $2.39 million in October, the largest annual increase since February 2018, according to the report released Monday.

The city’s rolling 12-month median also crossed the $2 million threshold for the first time since at least 2020, reaching $2.01 million — up 21% from a year earlier.

The luxury boom has been building for months. From March through June, at least 23 homes sold for more than $5 million each month, a level the city had never reached before this year.

The previous monthly records were six sales above $10 million in May and 30 above $5 million in June, both set in 2026.

The red-hot market has already produced some eye-popping deals.

Last month, a 112-year-old home near the Presidio sold for $15 million — nearly double its $7.99 million asking price — after attracting nine offers.

And just last week, a Gilded Age mansion at 2770 Broadway hit the market for $34.95 million, becoming the city’s priciest active listing of 2026.

Meanwhile, buyers are facing increasingly fierce competition for a shrinking pool of available properties.

A staggering 86% of single-family homes sold above ask in October, up from 77% a year earlier.

Homes spent an average of just 14 days on the market, the fastest October pace since at least 2019.

By month’s end, only 222 single-family homes remained for sale — down 20% from a year earlier and 41% from two years ago. That represented just 0.9 months of available inventory.

The surge marks a dramatic turnaround for a city that struggled with an exodus of residents during the pandemic, as remote work allowed tech employees to relocate elsewhere.

The price gains have spread across nearly every corner of the city, though some neighborhoods are seeing far bigger jumps than others.

Potrero Hill led the pack, with its rolling 12-month median sale price skyrocketing 55% to $2.55 million.

Eureka Valley–Dolores Heights followed with a 54% jump to $3.76 million, while the Inner Mission climbed 41% to $2.2 million.

All 31 neighborhoods with at least 25 single-family sales over the past year recorded increases in their 12-month median prices.

But the city’s more affordable neighborhoods saw relatively little movement. Bayview’s median barely budged, rising less than 1% to $955,000, while Outer Mission increased 2% to $1.2 million.

The condo market is also showing signs of renewed strength, though buyers appear more cautious.

The median condo sale price rose 12% year-over-year to $1.34 million in October, while 68% of units sold above asking, compared with 43% a year earlier.

Yet 18% of condo listings underwent price reductions during the month, up from just 5% a year earlier and the highest October share since at least 2020.

news.originalContent:
The country’s largest Muslim advocacy group urges Trump to address rising hate crimes against Muslims instead of attacking its efforts.

The largest Muslim civil liberties organisation in the United States has condemned suggestions by President Donald Trump that it could face a blanket designation as a “terrorist” group.

The Council on American–Islamic Relations (CAIR) said the White House should be addressing violence against American Muslims, rather than attacking the rights group.

“The Trump administration should focus on addressing this surge in violent hate, not entertaining smears against the civil rights organisation that counters such hate,” CAIR said in a statement to Al Jazeera on Tuesday.

On Monday, Trump said he was considering giving a blanket “terrorist” designation to the Muslim Brotherhood and that his administration was also looking at CAIR, which is already classified as a “terrorist” group in Texas and Florida.

“CAIR is another one we are watching,” he said of the organisation.

When asked if he was considering naming CAIR as a foreign “terrorist” group, he responded: “I’m not going to say that yet, but it could happen.”

In its statement, CAIR said that it was “fully prepared to defend our civil rights work and the broader American Muslim community from any new attempts to censor free speech, punish dissent or otherwise undermine the rule of law”.

“Our advocacy for justice here and abroad is the real reason that anti-Muslim and anti-Palestinian extremists spend so much time obsessing over our work,” it said.

Trump’s comments on Monday came during an exchange with reporters outside the White House, following a question about Egypt’s crackdown on the Muslim Brotherhood and whether Washington would consider a broader designation of the group.

Earlier this year, the Trump administration designated the Muslim Brotherhood chapters in Lebanon, Jordan and Egypt as foreign “terrorist” organisations.

Trump praised Egypt, where the Muslim Brotherhood originated, for cracking down on the group, indicating it did so at his request.

“Egypt has clamped down very hard on the Muslim Brotherhood, at my request,” he told reporters as he left the White House on Monday.

“Egypt did a great job,” Trump said.

news.originalContent:
The law targets the group’s financing and activities as renewed fighting threatens to derail efforts to end Yemen’s war.

Yemen’s parliament has unanimously approved a law designating the Houthis as a “terrorist organisation” and criminalising the group’s activities and financing, as fighting intensifies between the group and forces loyal to the internationally recognised government.

The vote, held over two sessions by videolink on Monday, comes seven years after the measure was first proposed. Parliament said it had deferred the bill, first tabled at a session in the city of Seiyun in April 2019, to give peace efforts a chance.

It noted that the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah, had attacked government-held areas of Yemen and Saudi Arabia, and accused the Iranian-backed group of brushing aside “all options for peace”.

Yemen’s cabinet approved the draft law on October 11. The country’s National Defence Council had designated the Houthis a “terrorist” organisation by executive decision in October 2022. The United States also lists the group as a “terrorist” organisation, and Saudi Arabia treats it as one.

According to the state-run Saba news agency, the legislation was formally submitted to Rashad al-Alimi, head of the Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council, on Tuesday to be signed into law.

It runs to 55 articles and designates the group – including all of its political, military and civilian formations – “a terrorist organisation” and a “rebellious faction”.

It also toughens penalties for offences including seizing state authority, besieging cities, attacking civilians, laying landmines and attacking international shipping. Certain offences would carry the death penalty.

The law also sets out procedures to identify, trace, freeze and confiscate assets linked to the group and its affiliated entities.

The vote comes amid months of renewed hostilities after several years of relative calm on Yemen’s front lines. In late June, the Houthis announced an escalation against government forces and Saudi Arabia, saying the move was aimed at lifting what the group describes as a “blockade”.

In early September, a Houthi ground offensive on the western coast gave the group control of parts of Taiz and Hodeidah governorates after government forces withdrew from the port city of Mocha and the strategic Bab al-Mandeb area.

Government forces launched an operation called “Dawn of Yemen” in early October to retake Houthi-held territory, including the capital, Sanaa. It initially made limited gains in recapturing territory lost on the Red Sea coast, but on Sunday, pro-government forces withdrew from those areas, allowing the Houthis to advance further.

Heavy fighting continues in Marib, al-Jawf and Lahij governorates, and the Houthis are pressing to take the city of Taiz, which the government and rights groups say is under a tight siege. The Houthis have also stepped up attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia, while the Saudi-led coalition says it is striking facilities that fund the group’s war effort.

The Houthis seized Sanaa in September 2014. United Nations-sponsored talks and regional mediation have failed to end the war since then.

Ismail al-Suhaili, a political science professor and senior researcher at the Mokha Center for Strategic Studies, said the law marks a shift towards a tougher government position after the failure of peace efforts. Moving the designation from an executive decision to parliamentary legislation gives it wider legal force, he said.

He said it could complicate future negotiations by shifting their focus from power-sharing towards restoring state institutions, disarmament and UN Security Council Resolution 2216.

Al-Suhaili warned that the law could put additional pressure on banks, traders and companies operating between government- and Houthi-controlled areas and deepen Yemen’s financial split. Donors and aid organisations could also become reluctant to work in Houthi-held areas, which could disrupt the delivery of essential supplies to civilians. The Houthis, he said, could respond with further military escalation or with countermeasures targeting government leaders.

Tawfiq al-Hamidi, head of the SAM Organization for Rights and Liberties, told Al Jazeera the law was “a late step” but provides a legal basis for holding those responsible for abuses to account and compensating victims.

While the law narrows the space for political negotiations in favour of military action, al-Hamidi said, it does not entirely rule out a future settlement.

news.originalContent:
France witnesses its third major public sector strike since September, as protests highlight wage and service concerns.

Demonstrators have gathered across France after unions called a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises, as protests over living standards and squeezed public services continue to roil the country.

France’s 5.8 million public sector employees were urged to mobilise on Tuesday after talks with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Friday failed to satisfy union demands for across-the-board pay rises, following last week’s minimum wage boost for private-sector workers.

It is the third united day of strikes and protests in the public sector since September, after a previous mobilisation earlier this month drew hundreds of thousands of workers and saw police fire tear gas as clashes broke out in several cities.

More unions joined the call to strike after Lecornu’s meeting, saying the government’s proposed measures did not address what they describe as an urgent pay and cost-of-living crisis. In Paris, a major rally was taking place in the east of the city, with dozens of other demonstrations planned nationwide.

Police sources told AFP that between 40,000 and 80,000 people were expected to demonstrate in the capital, and up to 300,000 across France. In Paris, university professor Nicolas Prevot said he was marching to defend human rights, protect public services and keep the far right from power in next year’s presidential election.

news.originalContent:
Online petition with more than 32,000 signatures demands the university ‘cancel Nathan Cofnas’s invitation to speak’.

Thousands of people have signed a petition and protests are planned at the University of Oxford against the appearance of Nathan Cofnas, an American academic and self-described “race realist” accused of racism.

Cofnas, who had accused the late Professor Jason Arday of plagiarism last July, is due to give a talk at Oxford’s Oriel College on Tuesday evening at an event organised by the Oxford Reform student society, which is linked to the far-right Reform UK party.

Cofnas has drawn controversy for years with his eugenics-linked views tying race to intelligence, writing that Black people were less intelligent than others in an article which led to his dismissal from his position at a college at Emmanuel College, Cambridge.

He was suspended as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University in Belgium in August after making plagiarism allegations against Arday, a Black Cambridge professor. Arday consistently denied allegations of plagiarism but acknowledged errors in his work.

Arday was later found dead in his home after resigning his post amid the ballooning scandal.

Cofnas was later allowed to resume some academic work at Ghent remotely, without teaching, while an investigation continued.

The Oxford Reform student society defended its event – titled “Is DEI Undermining Higher Education?”, referring to diversity, equity and inclusion – and said it is “committed to broadening participation in university life”.

In a statement, Oxford University said the event being hosted on its grounds “does not imply endorsement by the College of the views of its speakers”.

An online petition demanding the university “cancel Nathan Cofnas’s invitation to speak” has more than 32,000 signatures.

“Ideas platformed at Oxford do not stay in the lecture theatre”, the petition said.

He was suspended as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University in Belgium in August after making plagiarism allegations against Arday, a Black Cambridge professor. Arday consistently denied allegations of plagiarism but acknowledged errors in his work.

Arday was later found dead in his home after resigning his post amid the ballooning scandal.

Cofnas was later allowed to resume some academic work at Ghent remotely, without teaching, while an investigation continued.

The Oxford Reform student society defended its event – titled “Is DEI Undermining Higher Education?”, referring to diversity, equity and inclusion – and said it is “committed to broadening participation in university life”.

In a statement, Oxford University said the event being hosted on its grounds “does not imply endorsement by the College of the views of its speakers”.

An online petition demanding the university “cancel Nathan Cofnas’s invitation to speak” has more than 32,000 signatures.

“Ideas platformed at Oxford do not stay in the lecture theatre”, the petition said.

news.originalContent:
Hundreds hail Student List lawmakers as the new parliament meets for the first time.

Following the October 25 vote that upended Serbia’s political landscape, the new parliament is meeting for the first time in Belgrade.

The vote redrew Serbia’s parliamentary map as a grassroots, student-led movement won the largest single share, removing President Aleksandar Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS).

The Student List group was backed by 2.3 million citizens, altering the previous parliamentary arithmetic and balance of power. It holds a majority with 140 parliamentary seats in the 250-member parliament, compared with the Serbian Progressive Party’s 104.

Tuesday’s session is chaired by the oldest member of parliament until a new speaker is elected, assisted by the four youngest MPs from the largest electoral lists. Hundreds of supporters cheered the new lawmakers as they entered the National Assembly. The new speaker could be announced later on Tuesday.

The formal agenda follows a clear legal framework: verifying parliamentary mandates based on a report by the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK), taking the solemn oath of office, electing the speaker and deputy speakers, appointing the secretary-general, and forming parliamentary committees and permanent delegations to international bodies.

But beyond legal formalities, the political atmosphere is complex and large sections of the public have high expectations.

Political analyst Djordje Vukadinovic told Al Jazeera, “Everyone is eagerly awaiting it. I would avoid making any predictions, because with the current opposition structure, you never know what might happen or what stance they will take.”

He added, “What I do know is that this is only the beginning of establishing a new government, and I believe not everything will be wrapped up today.”

Ahead of the session, a group of students wrote to the new lawmakers, reminding them of their “serious” responsibilities.

“All of you are becoming members of parliament in the highest legislative body of the Republic of Serbia for the first time. And only that. Nothing more. The fact that the highest state offices have for decades been presented as ‘comfortable armchairs’ is a systemic flaw. The people elected you. We are the people. You are the people. Act accordingly,” warned the Student Plenum of the Higher School of Civil Engineering and Geodesy in Belgrade in an open letter.

Aleksandar Cupic, an incoming Student List MP and an assistant professor in engineering, said new lawmakers must demonstrate institutional maturity.

“We do not plan to speak about our candidate for five or 10 hours, because that is neither in the spirit of the values we will represent nor is it rational. We owe it to the citizens to proceed with electing the speaker of parliament,” Cupic told reporters ahead of the session.

He said political groups had been consulting one another in a more moderate atmosphere than reports have suggested.

The swearing-in session also marks the start of a critical political countdown – a 90-day constitutional deadline to elect a new government.

Should that expire without parliament voting in a new cabinet, Serbia’s constitution mandates the dissolution of the National Assembly and the calling of snap parliamentary elections.

The developments are being watched across the region, as well as in European and global political circles.

Observers say the new political leaders will have to govern the state and rebuild sustainable cooperation with neighbouring countries and the European Union – ties that have been strained in recent years.

Echoing that point, Student List representative Aleksandar Baucal told the international EU Enlargement Forum in Brussels that a peaceful transfer of power is only the start of a complex array of work.

“Changing power through non-violent and democratic means is only the first step,” Baucal said in Brussels. “Serbia now faces the task of rebuilding institutions that will prevent the personalisation of power and serve all citizens, regardless of who they voted for. I am convinced that from now on, the news coming out of Serbia will be largely positive.”

In a similar vein, the European Democratic Party (EDP) weighed in on the eve of the parliamentary session.

“Serbia must now heal the wounds of recent years through truth, justice and accountability … we sincerely hope a new chapter of freedom, democracy and reconciliation will begin,” the EDP said, adding that the session will test whether Serbia is ready for institutional reform.

news.originalContent:
A major health organisation declares measles endemic in US for first time since 2000, reversing decades of progress.

The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status, reversing a public health achievement maintained for 26 years, as the country grapples with its largest outbreak in more than three decades.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the Americas branch of the World Health Organization (WHO), declared measles endemic in the US, Bolivia, and Mexico on Tuesday after determining that the same strain of the virus had circulated continuously in the country for at least 12 months.

An international panel of experts that advises PAHO on the prevalence of measles and rubella “recommended that the measles elimination status be withdrawn,” said Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, “a recommendation which I have accepted.”

Measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000.

PAHO’s announcement follows a review of epidemiological and laboratory evidence submitted by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The US has recorded approximately 7,700 measles infections since the beginning of 2025, according to CDC figures.

It is the highest number of cases the country has seen in more than 30 years. The climbing numbers come as vaccine hesitancy has grown under Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has repeatedly cast doubt on the safety of vaccines despite scientific evidence to the contrary.

Before taking office, Kennedy claimed that no vaccine was “safe and effective” and promoted the discredited theory that vaccines cause autism.

To protect against illness, children are commonly given the measles vaccine in a combined shot with mumps and rubella vaccines, known by the acronym MMR.

But the vaccination rate among preschoolers in the US has fallen to about 92 percent, below the level experts say is needed to prevent major outbreaks.

As health secretary under US President Donald Trump, Kennedy has questioned the MMR vaccine’s ability to protect children.

He has suggested that the MMR’s effectiveness wanes by about 4.5 percent a year and said it contains “aborted fetus debris”, a claim experts have rejected as false.

The CDC has confirmed six measles-related deaths this year, but state health officials in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and New York have reported 10 deaths combined, a discrepancy that has fuelled tensions between federal and state health authorities over how measles fatalities are classified and counted.

Measles is considered highly infectious, and the WHO credits the virus with 95,000 deaths worldwide in 2024, mostly among children.

Matt Ferrari, a biology professor and director of Pennsylvania State University’s Center for Infectious Disease Dynamics, believes the loss of the US’s measles elimination status can serve as a wake-up call for public health officials.

“This should be a humbling statement for the United States,” Ferrari told Al Jazeera.

For much of his career, Ferrari has studied strategies to control measles in countries around the world. The US was previously seen as a model.

“It was a motivating achievement that we use to drive support for measles elimination programmes all around the world,” said Ferrari. “Now we need to be looking for expertise elsewhere because we haven’t been pulling our weight.”

Edwin Asturias, a professor of paediatrics, infectious disease and epidemiology at the University of Colorado, described the loss of status as a “stain” on the country’s public health programme.

“Measles cases are a signal that your immunisation programme and other systems within your public health services are having problems,” he told Al Jazeera.

Asturias said the US had the resources and experience to prevent the resurgence of the virus, pointing to its success in eliminating local measles transmission for more than a quarter of a century.

About 40 percent of current US measles cases are among adults older than 20, he said, highlighting the need to expand vaccination efforts.

Reaching these populations will require making vaccines available in workplaces, places of worship and other community settings, rather than relying solely on paediatricians and family doctors, Asturias explained.

The loss of elimination status also has implications beyond US borders, as measles can spread through international travel and migration.

“The United States is not, anymore, a place where you’re safe from measles,” Asturias told Al Jazeera. “If you’re a common person walking around with your children, you need to know now that measles has come to the country to stay unless something else is done.”

The risk is particularly concerning for unvaccinated people and those who cannot receive the vaccine, including those with weakened immune systems or undergoing cancer treatment.

Public health experts say the announcement should serve as a catalyst for a more extensive vaccination response.

While they do not expect PAHO’s announcement to prompt a significant change in federal policy, some hope it will spur action among state and local health departments.

Ferrari argued that the US should look to countries with experience containing measles outbreaks, including India, where community health workers visit households to identify children who may have missed vaccinations or whose families may be reluctant to vaccinate.

He also suggested that states may need to reconsider vaccination strategies, including whether to offer an earlier first or second dose to protect young children in areas where measles is circulating.

In the US, children are routinely given two doses of the MMR vaccine. The first dose is typically administered to children at 12 to 15 months of age and the second at four to six years, before they start school. Two doses are about 97 percent effective at preventing measles.

In countries where measles transmission is more widespread, the second MMR dose is often given between the ages of 18 and 24 months.

In June, Pennsylvania began recommending an additional early dose, called a “dose zero”, for infants aged six months and older in areas with sustained measles transmission. Ferrari said this is a perfect example of how states could adapt their approaches locally.

But the prospect of a broader shift in the federal response remains unlikely.

CDC Director Erica Schwartz said last week the agency would continue “doing the same exact thing” in terms of its measles response, if the US lost its elimination status.

For Asturias, the federal response so far raises concerns about whether the country has the public health leadership needed to reverse the outbreak.

“This is hard to see happen,” he said. “But at the same time it is predictable when you don’t have experts running a public healthcare system.”

news.originalContent:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Nvidia’s general counsel will appear before three joint House panels for closed-door testimonies in early December, three committees announced Tuesday.

Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will appear before the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party for transcribed interviews on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2. The former CEO resigned on Thursday following allegations that he had an affair with a Chinese spy.

House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast and Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party Chairman John Moolenaar said in a joint statement that they are seeking answers about Huang’s potential national security breach.

“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” the chairmen said. “The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal.” (RELATED: Jensen Huang Agrees To Testify Before Congress Over Relationship With Alleged Chinese Spy)

🚨🚨 Jensen Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will testify before the House Permanent Select Committee of Intelligence, the House Foreign Affairs Committee’s and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party on Dec. 1 and 2. Both testimonies will be transcribed. @DailyCaller

Huang agreed to testify Thursday about the alleged relationship with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese asset and former executive at Singapore-based tech firm Megaspeed, which had bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips. Nvidia formed a committee Tuesday to oversee its national security policies and compliance with U.S. export controls, CBS News reported.

Lawmakers and Secretary of Treasury Scott Bessent expressed concern that China is gaining access to the company’s advanced chips, which are critical to developing artificial intelligence (AI) models. The U.S. barred sales of Nvidia’s chips to China over national security concerns.

“Nvidia recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security,” Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia’s board of directors, said in a statement.

President Donald Trump was reportedly informed of Alice Huang’s ties to China in 2025 but took no action. The Department of Justice (DOJ) overtook the criminal investigation into Megaspeed following an email from Teter to the Commerce Department, The New York Times reported Monday.

House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast and Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party Chairman John Moolenaar said in a joint statement that they are seeking answers about Huang’s potential national security breach.

“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” the chairmen said. “The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal.” (RELATED: Jensen Huang Agrees To Testify Before Congress Over Relationship With Alleged Chinese Spy)

President Donald Trump was reportedly informed of Alice Huang’s ties to China in 2025 but took no action. The Department of Justice (DOJ) overtook the criminal investigation into Megaspeed following an email from Teter to the Commerce Department, The New York Times reported Monday.

news.originalContent:
US President Trump said the deals would prevent ‘coercion by any single foreign supplier’.

United States President Donald Trump says that members of the Quad, a security grouping of the US and three Indo-Pacific countries, have reached agreements aimed at securing supply chains of critical minerals.

Trump met India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi – the other Quad leaders – in the Philippines on Thursday.

“Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific,” Trump said in remarks ahead of the meeting in Manila.

During the meeting, Trump said the agreements on critical minerals aimed to prevent “coercion by any single foreign supplier”. He did not single out China, which dominates global rare earth supplies.

Trump later said the US would have “everything we need” on rare earths in 10 months.

“We are making rare earth at a level that we’ve never made before. We’re going to catch them [China] within 10 months,” he said.

China last year imposed restrictions on exports of rare earths amid a trade dispute with the US. In June, the two sides agreed a deal aimed at restoring the US’s access to China’s rare earth supplies.

In a statement after the leaders’ meeting, the Quad expressed “grave concerns” about “economic coercion”, including through arbitrary export restrictions.

While the statement did not name any country, the US and Japan have complained about China’s restrictions on ‌exports of rare earths vital to the manufacturing of everything from electric cars to mobile phones.

China has effectively shut off exports of key critical minerals to Japan for nearly a year as relations between Asia’s two largest economies have nosedived.

It was Trump’s first meeting of the Quad grouping – which his predecessor US President Joe Biden regarded as a signature foreign policy initiative.

Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at the Clinton Institute at University College Dublin, told Al Jazeera that the meeting suggested the Quad grouping had a “functioning relationship”.

“Given the damage to the Quad during the Trump administration, including the instability caused by Trump’s tariffs on India, and India’s response by diversifying, the Quad meeting and statements like this give reassurance that there is still a functioning relationship,” Lucas said. “I’m not sure I’d call it an alliance, as I don’t think the Trump folks believe in alliances.”

Trump also joined a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Manila on the first day of a three-day trip to Asia.

After the Philippines, Trump will travel to China and attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, where he is expected to hold a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.

The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs says the talks will focus on topics of “groundbreaking significance”, including “safeguarding world peace”.

Asked by reporters about a CNN report which claimed that US intelligence had determined Tehran was developing plans to use a so-called “dirty bomb” to target officials in the Trump administration, Trump said he was “looking into it”.

He said that if Iran posed an “imminent threat” to Washington, “they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before”.

He added that he “hoped” Iran did not pose a threat, but that he took such a scenario “very seriously” because “they happen to be crazy”.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghei said in a post on X that “Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations, including the recent claims published by The New York Times and the fabricated media narrative surrounding an alleged ‘dirty bomb’ propagated by CNN.”

news.originalContent:
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth is cracking down on dangerous military barracks conditions that have plagued American troops for decades, as he faces mounting political backlash and sinking approval ratings.

Hegseth has ordered military leaders to address emergency housing conditions within 24 hours or relocate affected service members, while giving the military departments five days to demonstrate compliance, according to a recent memo. The long-overdue crackdown comes as the secretary faces growing scrutiny over the unpopular Iran war and a potential impeachment vote, with a recent Common Defense poll of military members and veterans finding majorities disapproved of his leadership.

Fifty-four percent of active-duty U.S. service members and 64% of military family members disapproved of Hegseth, according to the October survey conducted for Common Defense by Change Research.

The Pentagon did not immediately respond to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s request for comment on why this matter is just being addressed now and what else the administration has done to resolve the issue. (RELATED: Iran War Sparks Explosive Town Hall Between Navy Brass, Military Families)

Why the rush on the Barracks? Immediate Action on Unacceptable Living Conditions in Unaccompanied Housing - Inspections of all barracks due by Monday https://t.co/ZESJk4x6ai

“Every Service member deserves a place to live that is clean, safe, and comfortable. The Military Departments must act with urgency to correct unacceptable living conditions, reinforce confidence that concerns will be addressed, and strengthen readiness,” Hegseth wrote in the Nov 10. memo.

By Nov 13., the memo was updated to require that all military branches report actions taken to improve living conditions to the newly formed Barracks Task Force. They are also required to provide a projected timeline to restore rooms to “habitable occupancy” and address any policy or resource barriers that require Pentagon resolution, per Military Times.

The Barracks Task Force is led by Medal of Honor recipient, and senior Hegseth advisor Dakota Meyer. Meyer has thus far visited seven bases to tour barracks and talk to service members living in them. He is slated to visit 30 by the end of December, Military Times reports.

Unlivable barracks conditions — including dirty tap water, methane gas leaks from cracked sewage pipes, and moldy bedrooms — have plagued the military for years.

This memo came at the same time the Iran war is rapidly losing support and one week after Hegseth faced a failed impeachment effort.

news.originalTitle: Sen. Cornyn Uses Final Months In Office To Block Trump Judicial Nominee
news.title: Sen. Cornyn Uses Final Months In Office To Block Trump Judicial Nominee
news.originalSummary:
Texas Republican Sen. John Cornyn abstained from expressing support for a Texas federal judgeship nominee selected by the Trump administration Monday, pushing for a different nominee instead.

Cornyn declined to express support for Assistant Attorney General T. Elliot Gaiser, head of the Department of Justice’s Office of Legal Counsel, by withholding the blue slip, according to multiple reports.
news.summary:

Cornyn declined to express support for Assistant Attorney General T. Elliot Gaiser, head of the Department of Justice’s Office of Legal Counsel, by withholding the blue slip, according to multiple reports.
news.originalContent:
Texas Republican Sen. John Cornyn abstained from expressing support for a Texas federal judgeship nominee selected by the Trump administration Monday, pushing for a different nominee instead.

Cornyn declined to express support for Assistant Attorney General T. Elliot Gaiser, head of the Department of Justice’s Office of Legal Counsel, by withholding the blue slip, according to multiple reports.

Cornyn’s decision not to submit the blue slip to the Senate Judiciary Committee sank Gaiser’s chance of appearing at a Judiciary Committee hearing Wednesday.

Gaiser, from Ohio, was selected without going through the typical senator-led screening process in Texas.

The district court nominee has tenuous ties to Texas, according to Bloomberg Law.

Cornyn recommended that the White House nominate former federal prosecutor Steve Fahey instead, an aide of Cornyn’s told the outlet.

A last-minute effort by US President Donald Trump to install as many judges as possible before Democrats take control of the US Senate is running into resistance from some fellow Republicans. https://t.co/cp5Iwh7x7u

Cornyn’s is in his final months in office, as he was defeated in the Republican senate primary by President Donald Trump-backed Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Cornyn joins the growing Republican resistance to the Trump administration’s efforts to infuse the judiciary with conservative judges before the Democrats take control of the U.S. Senate. (RELATED: 7 GOP Senators Move To Delay Thune’s Coronation After Midterm Massacre)

Outgoing Oklahoma Republican Sen. Alan Armstrong also blocked a nominee, expressing frustration at the Trump administration’s choices.

“We put up a lot of really qualified candidates that we sent to the White House, and they basically ignored that and just put through their one,” Armstrong said, according to Bloomberg Law.

Republican Arkansas Sens. John Boozman and Tom Cotton opposed US District Judge Lee Rudofsky’s nomination to the St. Louis-based 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals — a move that scored a rare success in forcing the Trump administration to replace Rudofsky with Arkansas Supreme Court Justice J. Cody Hiland as the White House’s nominee for the judgeship.

Outgoing Republican North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis backed the Arkansas duo, saying that in deciding judgeships for their states, senators deserve more “respect” from the Trump administration, the outlet added.

The White house has on occasion effectively told senators, “This is our guy, I hope you’ll get on board,” Tillis told reporters Tuesday.

“That’s not how it works here,” Tillis added. “They should expect they’re going to get this response.”

The Senate is prioritizing judicial confirmations while Republicans are still in control, Senate Majority Leader John Thune said.

“We expect all judicial nominees pending in the Senate to be confirmed this year,” a White House official said in a statement.

news.originalContent:
پنج کشور عضو اتحادیه اروپا قصد دارند سال آینده مرکزی برای اخراج مهاجران در روآندا راه‌اندازی کنند. این اقدام بخشی از تلاش گسترده‌تر آنها برای افزایش روند بازگرداندن مهاجران است. بر اساس بیانیه‌های دولت‌های هلند و دانمارک، انتظار می‌رود آلمان، دانمارک، اتریش، یونان و هلند در سال ۲۰۲۷ یک «مرکز بازگشت» راه‌اندازی کنند که آماده پذیرش افرادی باشد که از این کشورها به آنجا منتقل خواهند شد.

این کشورها اعلام کردند که این طرح شامل مهاجرانی خواهد شد که به‌طور غیرقانونی در کشورهای آن‌ها اقامت دارند و مشمول حکم اخراج شده‌اند. دولت هلند نیز می‌گوید که این مرکز می‌تواند جایگزینی برای مواردی باشد که امکان بازگرداندن افراد اخراج‌شده به کشور مبدأشان وجود ندارد.

به گفته این کشورهای اروپایی، افرادی که به روآندا منتقل می‌شوند، می‌توانند یا در جامعه میزبان ادغام شوند و اقامت خود را در آنجا ادامه دهند، یا به کشور خود بازگردند. این طرح شامل افرادی خواهد شد که تمام راه‌های قانونی برای دریافت اجازه اقامت در این پنج کشور را طی کرده و دیگر امکان قانونی برای ماندن ندارند.

این موضوع با توافق لغوشده بریتانیا با روآندا تفاوت دارد؛ توافقی که بر اساس آن قرار بود افراد به روآندا فرستاده شوند تا درخواست‌های پناهندگی آن‌ها در آنجا بررسی شود. چالش‌های حقوقی باعث شدند توافق بریتانیا هرگز به مرحله اجرا نرسد و سرانجام در سال ۲۰۲۴، دولت تازه‌روی‌کارآمده حزب کارگر آن را لغو کرد.

اما اکنون دفتر نخست‌وزیری بریتانیا احتمال پیوستن این کشور به طرح جدید را رد نکرده و اعلام کرده است که این برنامه را «با علاقه دنبال خواهد کرد».

این پنج کشور می‌گویند طرح انتقال مهاجران به خارج از اروپا با قوانین اتحادیه اروپا و حقوق بین‌الملل مطابقت دارد؛ اما نهادهای حقوق بشری معتقدند که چنین اقدامی ممکن است حقوق مهاجران را نقض کند.

روز دوشنبه ۱۶ نوامبر/۲۵ آبان، در یک کنفرانس خبری مشترک در وین، کریستیان اشتوکر، صدراعظم اتریش، گفت که هدف این پنج کشور، کاهش فشار بر نظام‌های پناهندگی اروپا و متوقف‌کردن فعالیت قاچاقچیانی است که سفرهای مرگبار از طریق دریای مدیترانه را سازمان‌دهی می‌کنند.

دولت هلند هم در بیانیه‌ای اعلام کرد که در مرحله نخست این توافق، تنها مردان مجرد به کشورهای خارج از اروپا فرستاده خواهند شد. هلند همچنین گفته تمرکز خود را بر افرادی خواهد گذاشت که از کشورهای مبدأ واقع در همان منطقه جغرافیایی روآندا می‌آیند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

وینسنت بیروتا، وزیر کشور روآندا، گفته است که کشورش متعهد به همکاری با شرکای اروپایی برای ارائه راه‌حلی «امن، قانونی و شرافتمندانه برای مهاجران» است.

پیش از اعلام رسمی این توافق، منابع دیپلماتیک به خبرگزاری فرانسه گفتند که انتظار می‌رود این مرکز در ابتدا به‌صورت آزمایشی فعالیت کند و میزبان حدود ۱۰۰ نفر باشد. بر این اساس، احتمال دارد هر یک از پنج کشور حدود ۲۰ مهاجر را به روآندا بفرستد.

کلمانتین دو مونتژوا، پژوهشگر ارشد بخش آفریقا در سازمان دیده‌بان حقوق بشر، در واکنش به این خبر گفته انتخاب روآندا به‌عنوان محل این مرکز نگران‌کننده است؛ زیرا این کشور سابقه‌ای شناخته‌شده در سرکوب مخالفان، بازداشت‌های خودسرانه، بدرفتاری با زندانیان و حمایت از شورشیان مسلح در جمهوری دموکراتیک کنگو، کشور همسایه خود، دارد.

او گفت: «پرداخت پول به دولت کیگالی برای میزبانی از یک برنامه اخراج مهاجران، نه‌تنها موجب رنج و آسیب‌دیدن افرادی خواهد شد که به آنجا فرستاده می‌شوند، بلکه منابع مالی و اهرم فشار سیاسی در اختیار دولتی قرار می‌دهد که مسئول نقض جدی حقوق بشر، هم در داخل کشور خود و هم در خارج از آن است.»

با نزدیک‌شدن انتخابات در چندین کشور عضو اتحادیه اروپا، دولت‌ها تحت فشار قرار گرفته‌اند تا نشان دهند توانایی کنترل مهاجرت را دارند. بر اساس آمار آژانس اروپایی گارد مرزی و ساحلی، در ۱۰ ماه نخست سال ۲۰۲۶ نزدیک به ۱۱۰ هزار مورد عبور غیرقانونی از مرزهای اتحادیه اروپا ثبت شده است. این رقم در مقایسه با مدت مشابه سال قبل، ۲۹ درصد کاهش نشان می‌دهد.

در ماه اکتبر گذشته، حدود ۱۸ هزار و ۱۰۰ مورد عبور از مرزهای اروپا شناسایی شد که تقریباً ۶ درصد کمتر از اکتبر ۲۰۲۵، اما ۲۲ درصد بیشتر از ماه سپتامبر بود. به گفته این آژانس، افزایش اخیر عمدتاً به دلیل رشد چشمگیر ورود مهاجران از مسیر غرب آفریقا به سمت جزایر قناری بوده است.

پنج کشور عضو اتحادیه اروپا قصد دارند سال آینده مرکزی برای اخراج مهاجران در روآندا راه‌اندازی کنند. این اقدام بخشی از تلاش گسترده‌تر آنها برای افزایش روند بازگرداندن مهاجران است. بر اساس بیانیه‌های دولت‌های هلند و دانمارک، انتظار می‌رود آلمان، دانمارک، اتریش، یونان و هلند در سال ۲۰۲۷ یک «مرکز بازگشت» راه‌اندازی کنند که آماده پذیرش افرادی باشد که از این کشورها به آنجا منتقل خواهند شد.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Cindy Ord/Getty Images for Teen Vogue)

Prominent Right-wingers critical of President Donald Trump clashed over the weekend regarding what it means to be an anti-Trump conservative as the movement grapples with the Democrats’ blue wave in the midterms and the approaching end of the Trump era.

The exchange began Thursday after a video surfaced of Sarah Longwell, co-founder of Republican advocacy group Defending Democracy Together and founder and publisher of The Bulwark, describing herself as a “lib” while celebrating the Democrats’ election victory at the “What’s Next” conference hosted by the Majority Democrats group last Thursday, Nov. 12 in Denver, Colorado. (RELATED: Trump’s White House Counsel Draws Line Against Dems’ Potential Abuse Of Power After Congress Flips Blue)

“You may know us; we’re the Never Trumpers. At least we were ten years ago. Now we’re just kind of libs, just like the rest of you,” Longwell said, attempting to get the crowd animated.

The video prompted a response from Babylon Bee writer Frank Fleming, who asked who is crazier: “People who surrendered all their principles to always agree with Trump or people who surrendered all their principles to always oppose him?”

The Bulwark’s Sarah Longwell at Democrat conference: "You may know us, we’re the Never Trumpers. At least we were ten years ago. Now we’re just kind of libs just like the rest of you." Yes, we know. https://t.co/ikdUQdUyHU

Jonah Goldberg, editor-in-chief of the center-right, Never Trump digital media company, argued that both the Always Trump and Never Trump mentalities were two sides of the same coin.

Longwell took issue with the comparison, responding to Goldberg by framing “anti-anti Trumpers and far leftists as two sides of the same coin.”

She argued that both groups understood Trump’s opponent in the 2024 election, Democratic Vice President Kamala Harris, “would be better for the country than Trump,” but Republicans critical of Trump “refused to say so and spent their energy shitting on normie dems.”

“And now that Trump is catastrophic, they’re all trying to wave away the role their moral ambivalence played in getting us here,” Longwell continued. “This is all just classic ‘People will forgive you for being wrong, but they’ll never forgive you for being right.’”

Goldberg fired back Sunday, calling Longwell a “political operative” who would “say or do what’s necessary for your team to win.”

I walked away from this stupid spat for a day. So I missed this. Sarah, if you honestly think this “anti-anti Trump” sophomoric bullshit is a thoughtful or clever response to me or description of how I’ve behaved the last decade, I honestly think you are so deep in your bubble that any and all of your political and moral judgement is simply worthless. I don’t even want to bother arguing with you, I’m more embarrassed for you than anything else. But I’ll engage one more time. Look, the reason for the Bulwark’s current orientation is evaporating as we’re reaching the end of the Trump era. It appears to me and everybody else that during your bow-taking moment the other day you tried to advance your rebranding when you told a room full of conventional progressive Dems that you were a “lib” just like them. People noticed. They pointed out that you conceded the central criticism of your project. But as you still need to hold onto some vestige of your “conserving conservatism” schtick you tried to clean up your remarks by suggesting you meant “classical liberal.” Literally no one believes that’s what you meant, including obviously the people in that room, and I doubt many believe you’re a classical liberal (is there a chapter of “Classical Liberals For Abdul Syed” I missed?). The way you frame this makes my point, not yours. You’re a political operative. You think, like a political operative, that you should say or do what’s necessary for your team to win. That’s entirely defensible for political operatives and party hacks (within reason, I have no patience for Trump apologists and hacks. I can show you the receipts if you don’t believe me). But here’s the point: I’m neither a political operative nor party hack. Kamala Harris would have been better than Trump, happy to say it. But you pretty clearly think that means I should have become a partisan for her and spin for her and Democrats the way you do. I don’t want to be a partisan hack. It’s not for me. But you cannot even comprehend such motives. All you have is a hammer and so everything is a nail to you. Projecting your self-serving bullshit on me doesn’t mean it’s not bullshit, no matter how good it makes you feel. I’m glad I could clear this up for you.

While Goldberg stressed that he had no patience for Trump apologists and hacks, he distinguished himself as “neither a political operative nor party hack.”

“Kamala Harris would have been better than Trump, happy to say it. But you pretty clearly think that means I should have become a partisan for her and spin for her and Democrats the way you do. I don’t want to be a partisan hack. It’s not for me. But you cannot even comprehend such motives,” Goldberg said. “All you have is a hammer, and so everything is a nail to you. Projecting your self-serving bullshit on me doesn’t mean it’s not bullshit, no matter how good it makes you feel.”

The back-and-forth involved plenty of personal attacks, but the dispute goes beyond a personality clash. It exposes an existential crisis of purpose and business models within the fracturing Never Trump movement, as the political glue that has held it together approaches its expiration date.

As the Trump era moves closer to its end, each faction of the movement must look toward 2028 and decide whether to maintain its existing alliances or adapt to whatever emerges as the new political landscape.
